topic.name: Defining the Derivative Using Derivative Notation

question.text: Given the curve $y = 5x-4x^2$, calculate $y'(x)$ using the definition of the derivative.
question.explanation:
Let $f(x)= 5x-4x^2.$ The definition of $y'(x)$ is \begin{align*} y'(x) = \lim_{h\rightarrow 0}\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}. \end{align*}

Applying this to $f(x)= 5x-4x^2$, we get

\begin{align*} f'(x) &=\lim_{h\rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{\left(5(x+h)-4(x+h)^2\right) - (5x-4x^2)}{h}\right)\\[2pt] &=\lim_{h\rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{5x +5h -4x^2 -8xh -4h^2 - 5x+4x^2}{h}\right)\\[2pt] &=\lim_{h\rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{ h(5-8x-4h) }{h}\right)\\[2pt] &=\lim_{h\rightarrow 0}\left(5-8x-4h\right)\\[2pt] &= 5-8x-4(0)\\[2pt] &= 5-8x. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating the Derivative of a Function

question.text: Use the definition of the derivative to find $f'(x)$ if $f(x) = -5x^2+2.$
question.explanation:
The definition of $f'(x)$ is

\begin{align*} f'(x) = \lim_{h\rightarrow 0}\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}. \end{align*}

Applying this to $f(x)=-5x^2+2$, we get

\begin{align*} f'(x) &=\lim_{h\rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{-5(x+h)^2+2 - (-5x^2+2)}{h}\right)\\[2pt] &=\lim_{h\rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{-5(x^2+2xh+h^2)+2 +5x^2-2)}{h}\right)\\[2pt] &=\lim_{h\rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{-5x^2-10xh -5h^2+2 +5x^2 - 2}{h}\right)\\[2pt] &=\lim_{h\rightarrow 0}\left(\frac{-10xh -5h^2 }{h}\right)\\[2pt] &=\lim_{h\rightarrow 0}\frac{h(-10x -5h)}{h}\\[2pt] &=\lim_{h\rightarrow 0}\left(-10x -5h\right)\\[2pt] &= -10x. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating the Derivative of a Function

question.text: Given that $f(x) = -7x^3$, what is $f'(x)$ according to the definition of the derivative?
question.explanation:
The derivative $f '(x)$ is given by the limit

\[ \lim_{h\to 0}\left(\dfrac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}\right). \]

Since $f(x) = -7x^3$, we have that $f(x+h) = -7(x+h)^3.$ Hence, we get

\begin{align} \displaystyle f'(x)&=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\dfrac{-7(x+h)^3-(-7x^3)}{h}\right) \\[3pt] &=\lim_{h\to 0}\left(\dfrac{-7(x+h)^3+7x^3}{h}\right). \end{align}
